correlates.name: Primary Aldosteronism
correlates.presentation: the triad of hypertension, unexplained hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis.
correlates.pathophysiology: primary mineralocorticoid excess, specifically aldosterone, driving sodium retention with potassium and hydrogen ion loss.

correlates.name: Renal Artery Stenosis and Fibromuscular Dysplasia
correlates.presentation: an abdominal bruit heard on abdominal auscultation is the exam clue for both.
correlates.pathophysiology: renovascular narrowing lowers renal perfusion, which stimulates renin and drives the RAAS cascade above.

correlates.name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
correlates.pathophysiology: disordered breathing during sleep; a recognized secondary cause of hypertension.

correlates.name: Resistant Hypertension
correlates.presentation: blood pressure remaining >= 140/90 despite optimal use of 3 or more antihypertensive medications of different classes, including a diuretic at maximally tolerated dose - or blood pressure controlled only on 4 or more medications…

correlates.name: Hypertensive Emergency
correlates.presentation: >= 180/>= 120 plus acute end-organ damage. Search for encephalopathy or stroke; retinal hemorrhages or papilledema; myocardial infarction, heart failure, or aortic dissection; acute kidney injury.

correlates.name: Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis
correlates.pathophysiology: chronically increased pressure narrows the afferent and efferent arterioles, which reduces glomerular blood flow and produces glomerular and tubular ischemia, then nephrosclerosis and fibrosis.
